title: Bourbon Vanilla Tallow Balm: My Skin Stopped Freaking Out This Spring
body:
My face felt like paper. That weird, tight paper. You know the kind. It was April, I think. Maybe late March. The weather couldn't decide. One day it’s 60 and sunny, the next it’s 40 with this wind that just… scrapes you. My skin just gave up. It was flaky in some spots, weirdly oily in others, and just generally pissed off. Classic spring skincare chaos. I was sitting there, my chair was cold because the heat clicked off, and I just thought, *this is stupid*. I’d tried everything for my dry spring skin. Everything. The expensive stuff in the frosted glass jars. The drugstore lotions that smell like a flower shop exploded. Nothing stuck. It all just sat on top or made me feel greasy. Then I saw someone talking about beef tallow balm. For your face. I stared at my phone. Beef fat. On my face. It sounded like something my great-grandmother would have used, not a thing you buy on the internet in 2024. But my skin was so mad. I was desperate. So I ordered this Whipped Tallow Balm in Bourbon Vanilla from some little shop on Etsy. I figured, worst case, I’m out thirty bucks and I have a weird story.

Anyway. It showed up.

## Why I Even Tried Beef Tallow on My Face

Look. I get it. It sounds gross. My first thought was literally, “I’m gonna smell like a kitchen.” Or a cowboy. I don’t know. But I kept reading. This stuff isn’t just… fat. It’s from grass-fed cows, whipped up into this cream. They make it in France, which felt fancy for beef fat. The big thing people kept saying is that it’s similar to the oils our own skin makes. Our sebum. So instead of just coating your skin with some synthetic silicone thing, it actually sinks in because your skin recognizes it. Or something. I’m not a scientist. I just know my moisturizer wasn’t moisturizing. It was just… there. I was dealing with these little dry patches that no amount of exfoliating would fix, and this lingering tightness from winter that just wouldn’t quit, even though it was technically spring. My spring skincare routine was a graveyard of failed products. So I opened the jar.

It did not smell like a kitchen.

It smelled like… vanilla. But not like cake. Or candles. It was warmer. Deeper. Bourbon vanilla, they call it. It’s cozy. It’s the scent equivalent of a thick sweater. Stress-reducing? I don’t know about that, but it definitely didn’t stress me out. The texture was weird. In a good way. It’s solid but soft. You scoop a little with your finger and it melts immediately. Like, before you even get it to your face. It just becomes this oil. I rubbed it between my palms first, like you’re supposed to, and then just… patted it on. On my still-damp face after washing it. I braced for grease.

It wasn’t greasy.

It was… nothing. It was like my skin drank it. I mean, there was a slight sheen for a minute, but it was gone fast. My face just felt… calm. Not tight. Not papery. Not slick. Just normal. I didn’t look shiny. I looked like I had skin. That was new. I sat there for a second waiting for the clogged pores to announce themselves. They never did.

## What This Tallow Balm Actually Does (For Me, Anyway)

So my routine now is stupid simple. Which is good because I’m lazy. At night, I wash my face. Sometimes with a cleanser, sometimes just with water if I didn’t wear makeup. My cat was watching me do this the other night, judging me hard. Then, while my skin’s still a little wet, I take a tiny scoop of this bourbon vanilla tallow balm. Tiny. Like, half the size of a pea. Rub my hands together, pat it all over. That’s it. I don’t do ten steps. I don’t have serums. I just have this jar.

The change wasn’t overnight. But after a few days, I noticed the flakiness was just… gone. The tight feeling when I smiled? Gone. The weird oily patches on my nose and forehead balanced out. It was like my skin finally got what it needed and stopped panicking. I started using it on my hands too. Because why not. I wash my hands a million times a day, and they get these little cracks at the knuckles in the spring. It’s the worst. A little of this balm at night, and my hands are actually soft in the morning. Not “lotion soft” that washes off, but actually better.

Here’s the unrelated observation: using this stuff forces you to slow down for a second. You can’t just squirt it and run. You have to scoop it, let it melt in your hands, warm it up, press it in. It’s a thirty-second ritual. I usually do it while my tea is steeping. It’s become this little pocket of quiet. I’m not saying it’s spiritual. It’s beef fat. But the *act* of using it is weirdly calming. The scent helps. It’s not perfume-y. It’s just… nice.

I got curious and used it on a little patch of eczema I sometimes get on my arm. I don’t want to over-promise, but it calmed down way faster than it usually does. The itching stopped. The skin just looked less angry. I’m not saying it’s a cure, but for my dry spring skin and its various complaints, it’s been a game-changer. A very simple, very weird game-changer.

## Would I Buy This Tallow Balm Again?

I’m on my second jar. That’s the answer, I guess. I ordered the first one out of pure, frustrated curiosity. I ordered the second one because I ran out and my skin started feeling like paper again when I stopped using it for a week. That was all the proof I needed.

I even told my mom about it. She’s in her 60s and has always had dry skin. She was even more skeptical than I was. “Beef tallow? Really?” But she tried it when she was visiting. She used it for two days and then asked me for the link to the Etsy shop. Now she uses it too. She says it helps with the fine lines around her eyes because it’s so nourishing without being heavy. Her word, not mine. I just know it works.

It’s not magic. If you’re expecting to look 25 again, this isn’t it. But if your skin is dry, or sensitive, or just confused by the season—if you have that classic spring dryness where nothing seems to hydrate it—this tallow balm for spring might actually help. It fixed that winter damage hangover for me. It just makes my skin feel resilient. Like it can handle the wind and the weird temperature swings. It feels strong. I don’t know how else to put it.

I got mine from this shop on Etsy called… I forget the full name. Malti something. The jar is simple. The label is cute. It came pretty fast. That’s all I know. I’m just a person who bought a thing.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, I think so. It was for mine. The science-y reason is that it’s really similar to the oils our skin makes naturally, so it absorbs well and doesn’t just sit on top. It’s like giving your skin something it already knows how to use. People have been using animal fats on their skin forever, apparently. We just forgot.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
It hasn’t clogged mine, and my skin is pretty picky. Because it absorbs and isn’t just a layer of grease, it doesn’t seem to cause problems. It’s non-comedogenic, which means it shouldn’t clog pores. My experience says that’s true.

**What does Bourbon Vanilla tallow balm smell like?**
It smells like vanilla, but not the sweet, ice cream kind. It’s warmer. More like vanilla extract you’d cook with, but smoother. It’s cozy. It doesn’t smell like beef at all, which was my biggest worry. The scent fades pretty quickly after you put it on, too. You’re not walking around smelling like a bakery.

So yeah. That’s my tallow thing. My skin’s happy. I’m happy. For this spring, at least, the paper-face feeling is gone. If your skin is being difficult with the season change, it might be worth a shot. I didn’t expect much from a jar of whipped beef fat, but honestly? It just works.
